description: The same rush team on both sides of a 6-row gap: the battle stays symmetric.
A rush (two barracks) against a base with only a wall and its Core; soldiers walk across and destroy the Core.
A Core walled in on all sides (one weak wall, tier 1): the soldiers break through the weakest wall and reach the Core.

A Core ringed by eight tier 1 walls and two soldiers walking in from the gap: the battle is saved and restored (JSON round trip) after 50, 95, 130 and 200 ticks (before and after the first wall takes damage, and after it falls), and ends exactly like an uninterrupted run (the breach field depends only on the saved state).

Three raiders (placed at tick 0) walk past the extractor and the splitter of a base to its Core (issue #66: no unit prefers buildings): nothing is destroyed, the barracks downstream keeps producing, and the two sides fight at the Core.

Three powered tier 2 turrets beside the front edge kill three soldiers that cross it after a long walk across a 12-row gap, by which time the turrets are charged (they fire once a unit stands on their own board rows or in the neutral zone).
Three powered tier 3 turrets on the front row shoot and kill a soldier that is still in the 12-row neutral zone (PP-13): it never reaches the turret owner's board rows.
The same three turrets without any supply never fire; the soldiers walk in and attack the Core.

A wall line with one gate: a soldier inside walks out through the gate (standing on its cell) while an enemy soldier outside cannot enter and attacks the gate, until the owning soldier comes out and kills it.
Eight tier 1 turrets; a lake band and walls leave a single approach (x = 8) right above them, so a twelve-soldier wave runs the gauntlet.

A fast flux extractor feeds a tier 1 overclocker (costPerStep 2, +2 percent per step); the ore extractor beside it, which feeds a barracks, speeds up step by step (ore items at 19, 39, 58, 77, 96, ...).

Two plots. Player 0 has the ore extractor and barracks and the flux extractor feeding a tier 1 overclocker (as in ramp-overclocker-speeds-source); player 1 has a lone ore extractor in their own plot (ore node at x 12, not connected, so its items are lost at its own cadence) and no overclocker. Player 0's collectors speed up step by step; player 1's extractor stays on the unmodified cadence (PP-8).
An armory (costPerStep 4, +5 percent per step) beside a barracks: the soldiers spawned at ticks 99, 199 and 299 have 42, 44 and 46 health; units already on the field keep theirs.

A tier 1 overclocker (maxSteps 5) fed by a fast flux extractor takes its fifth and last step at tick 179 and then takes nothing more: 14 items are delivered in all (10 spent on the five steps, 4 left in its full buffer) and the extractor stalls, first at tick 119 and again at tick 159.

A base sealed by a wall row whose weakest point is an overclocker (a tier 2 flux extractor feeds it): the attackers breach it and destroy it at tick 209, just after its fifth and last step (tick 187); its bonus leaves the total at once.
Two Cores in wall rings and no producers: Overload decay (5 * level on every 100th tick from 1800) destroys both Cores at tick 3100 (cumulative 525 >= 500).

A Core ringed by six tier 3 walls and a soldier standing on the corner cell beside two of them (buildings 4 and 5, equal in everything but current health: building 5 starts at 20 of 240). The breach step prices a building by its maximum health, so both cost the same and the tie goes to building 4; the soldier never touches the damaged building 5 (a rule that used current health would chew through it).

Four soldiers of side 0 walk towards one stationary enemy (a unit_post): two start the same distance from it on either side, two at different distances. Overlapping units are pushed apart; the state hash pins every position.

Twelve soldiers of side 0 cross a wall line with a single one-cell gap (board row 8 of side 1). They crowd the gap, push through it (overlapping a little while they squeeze) and slide along the wall; the invariant (nothing inside a wall) holds on every tick, and the positions after 300 ticks are pinned.

A tier 1 barracks is walled in except for one cell, and a unit_post of its own side stands on that cell (held in place because an enemy unit_post in contact with it keeps both busy attacking): the finished unit cannot be placed, so the barracks holds it, stops drawing from its input buffer (the conduit backs up and the extractor stalls) and nothing is spawned in 700 ticks.

An ogre (collision radius 160, diameter 320 > one cell) and a soldier of side 0 head for a wall line with a one-cell gap: the soldier, nearer to the gap, passes and goes on to the Core; the ogre waits in front of the gap (the circle rules, not the cell field, stop it). Positions after 500 ticks are pinned.

Nine groups, apart from each other. In eight, a fast dart (side 0 or 1) aggroes on a stationary post of the other side whose centre it reaches in one step, so the two centres coincide; the unit ids give odd and even sums, the mover the higher or the lower id. In the ninth, two darts of equal priority reach the same post. Each pushed unit leaves along the separation axis in the frame of its own side (side 1 mirrors side 0); a harmless pin of the dart side keeps each post in contact (so anchored) without blocking the push. The positions pin the rule.

Four players per side, Cores only. One soldier of side 0 from each plot walks to the Core of the plot opposite its own and attacks it: all four enemy Cores take damage (a single shared goal would hit only one).

The same four soldiers with the enemy Cores of players 2 and 3 nearly dead. When a unit's Core falls it takes the nearest remaining Core (unit_retargeted) and keeps it; units whose Core still stands do not change.
The four-plot retarget battle saved and restored before, during and after the first Core falls: the result equals the run without restoring.
Two players per side. The soldier of plot 0 walks to Core 1 and destroys it; it then takes Core 0 as its target.

The soldier of plot 1 destroys Core 2, standing above it. Cores 1 and 3 are exactly as far from it (movement distance 104 each); the tie is broken by the plot nearer to the opposite one (equal) and then the larger player index, so it takes Core 3.

A soldier of plot 0 (target: Core 3, at the far left) stands beside Core 2, which is not its target. It attacks Core 2 as an enemy in reach and holds its place until Core 2 falls, then walks on to Core 3 and attacks that; its target never changes.

The same four-player team with a working barracks line in every plot on both sides of a 4-row gap, Cores 0 and 3 weak: the battle stays mirror-symmetric through the falls and retargets (checked tick by tick in unit-targets.test.ts).

A base sealed by a wall row whose weak point is the extractor that sends over a border link: the attackers destroy it, and both halves of the link go with it (two conduit_destroyed events, in id order; the vector pins only hashes, the events are checked by border-battle.test.ts). It is saved and restored at ticks 100 and 300, around the cut.

A base sealed by a wall row whose weak point is the barracks that receives over a border link: the attackers destroy it, and both halves of the link go with it, so the extractor on the other plot loses its path.

Player 0 loses their Core early (health 1) while their extractor still sends over a border link to the barracks of player 1: no building or conduit is destroyed by the fall, and the link keeps delivering until the end.

An archer and a soldier of side 0 start in the same row, five cells apart, and walk at the enemy Core. The archer stops short of it (the gap to the Core is about three cells) and shoots (reach 720 is edge to edge) and holds its place for the rest of the run; the soldier walks up against the Core. Positions after 300 ticks are pinned.

A lake line spans the whole enemy board (board row 8). A soldier and a drone of side 0 start in front of it: the soldier cannot cross and stays in front of the lake; the drone flies over it, never needs a breach, and attacks the Core (flyers ignore walls and lakes). Positions after 400 ticks are pinned.

A soldier and an archer of side 0 meet a drone and a soldier of side 1 in the middle of the field. Melee units cannot hit a flyer, so the soldiers fight each other while the archer and the drone shoot at each other and at the soldiers; by tick 200 both units of side 1 and one of side 0 are dead. Positions are pinned.

Soldiers, archers, drones and a raider on both sides, mirrored half a turn, behind two lake lines with gaps: the battle is saved and restored (JSON round trip) after 7, 111 and 250 ticks and ends exactly like an uninterrupted run; the sides stay mirror images (checked tick by tick in ranged-flyers.test.ts).

A Hangar is walled in completely (walls on every side, its only other side taken by the conduit from the Extractor). Its drones appear on the cells next to it, fly out over the walls and attack the enemy Core. A Barracks in the same spot holds its unit (see producer-held-at-blocked-exit). Positions after 1500 ticks are pinned.

Side 1 has a full wall line on board row 8 and a row of six Barracks behind it on board rows 5 and 6. A soldier and a drone of side 0 start in front. The drone flies over walls and buildings without attacking any of them and shoots the Core; the soldier has to breach. Positions after 400 ticks are pinned.

Three plots; side 1 has a lake line across the whole board (board row 8), so the ground fields rank every Core alike. A drone of the middle plot shoots down the middle Core (hp 1) at once, then picks the next Core by straight-line distance (the near one on its right), where the ground tie rule would pick the higher index (the far one on its left). Positions after 300 ticks and the event log are pinned.

A tier 3 Foundry fed by a tier 3 Ore collector and a tier 3 Power collector spawns a heavy unit every 50 ticks once both counters are full (the first at tick 5 + 50 once Ore and Power have arrived); the heavies march on the enemy Core. Positions after 1000 ticks are pinned.
The same Foundry with only its Ore input connected never spawns: no unit exists after 800 ticks.

A Foundry and a Barracks (both tier 3) share the Ore of one tier 3 collector through a splitter; the Foundry also has its own Power collector. Soldiers and heavies both march on the enemy Core; the saved and restored run (ticks 150 and 400) continues exactly like the original.
Player 1 Foundry gets its Power over a border link from player 0 and its Ore from its own collector; it spawns heavy units owned by player 1. Saved and restored at tick 200.

A sealed base behind two wall rows with a tier 1 Foundry as the weak point (it spans both rows; its Power collector stands outside and sends through a conduit in the second row): the Foundry holds Power only (its Power counter is full, Ore never arrives, so it never produces); the attackers destroy it, then the rest of the base is breached. Its conduit goes with it (Mid-battle removal); the battle is saved and restored at ticks 100 and 300.

Two tier 3 collectors feed a tier 3 Composite refinery whose output feeds a test unit producer (extraBuildings: no shipped building takes Composite yet); it spawns soldiers from the Composite. Saved and restored at tick 300.
The same chain with the Aether refinery (Power south, Flux west) and a test producer that takes Aether.

A sealed base behind two wall rows with a tier 2 Composite refinery as the weak point (it spans both rows; Power from a collector outside, Ore from a collector inside). Its output goes straight into a test consumer that makes one unit and then waits 100000 ticks (extraBuildings), so after four batches (tick 156) six items are absorbed and the refinery is stalled holding two. The attackers destroy it at tick 198: the two items in its output store are lost (two `lost` events), its three conduits go with it and nothing more reaches the consumer (Mid-battle removal); the battle is saved and restored at ticks 100 and 300.

The full chain: a tier 3 Ore collector and a tier 3 Power collector feed a tier 3 Composite refinery, whose output feeds a tier 3 Golem forge; Golems (armor 3) walk with the soldiers of a Barracks against a base that makes soldiers. Saved and restored mid-battle.
The turret-kills-wave scenario with three Golems instead of soldiers: each turret shot is reduced by the Golem armor (3), so the turrets need more shots.

A Golem (collision diameter 160, under one cell) and a soldier of side 0 cross a wall line with a single one-cell gap: both pass, the Golem pushing and being pushed by the soldier under the soft-collision rules.

A Golem of side 0 meets a soldier, an archer and a raider of side 1 at the front: the soldier hits for 3 (6 - 3), the archer for 2 (5 - 3), the raider for 5 (8 - 3); the Golem hits for 6 (the soldiers have no armor).

The full chain: a tier 3 Power collector and a tier 3 Flux collector feed a tier 3 Aether refinery, whose output feeds a tier 3 Spire; casters (splash 50 percent within one cell) walk alone against a base that makes soldiers. Saved and restored mid-battle.

A caster shoots a soldier in a tight group: neighbours within one cell (a soldier, a drone, a Golem, whose armor cuts its share to 1) take 50 percent of the hit, the soldier 241 away and the caster's own soldier do not.
Casters against a closed wall line: they hit the wall (a building), so there is no splash event.

Each side has a targeted strength modifier: side 0 Sharpshooters (+25% archer), side 1 Vanguard (+20% soldier and raider). Each side fields an archer and a soldier at the same cells; only the listed types are stronger, so the battle is not symmetric (the state hash and Core health pin the numbers).

A guard soldier holds a point on the zone's middle row (row 19). A soldier of side 0 walks up column 1, five cells from the point: outside the 3 cells of aggro, it is not drawn in, nobody attacks the guard and the guard does not move. The run is also saved and restored mid-way.

A soldier of side 0 starts three cells from a guard archer: inside aggro range it walks up, fights and kills the single guard (unit_died with side 2, one guard killed for side 0) and survives; nothing counts as a unit death of a side.

A guard soldier stands 4.5 cells from its point, beyond the 3-cell leash, with a soldier of side 1 right next to it. While beyond the leash the guard drops its target (it does not attack) and walks back along the movement field to the point while the enemy hits it; once inside the leash it fights back. The enemy wins the duel and the kill is credited to side 1; positions are pinned.

Two points, a guard archer at one and a guard soldier at the other, each with a drone of side 0 two cells away. The archer hits its drone; the soldier cannot hit its drone (only ranged attackers hit flyers) while the drone shoots it.

Three powered tier 3 turrets on the front row (as in turret-kills-in-zone) with a guard soldier two cells in front of them, well in range, in the zone: no turret ever fires (a guard is not an enemy of a side's buildings).

A guard soldier and a guard archer on one point, a soldier of side 0 two cells south of it and a soldier of side 1 two cells north: both sides fight the guards (and the guards fight back) rather than each other; the kills are credited to the side that dealt the most damage.

A point on the zone's middle row (row 19, column 8) with no guards. A soldier of side 0 walks up column 1, seven cells from it: outside the 3 cells of point aggro it never diverts, nothing is captured and the point stays uncontrolled.

A point (row 19, column 6) with no guards. A soldier of side 0 passes two cells away on its way to the enemy Core at column 1, diverts, stops within the capture radius of 2 cells and captures in captureTicks (50): point_capture_started, then point_captured 49 ticks later (previous -1). It then resumes its march. Saved and restored once.
The same point with three soldiers of side 0 in range from tick 0: progress grows by 3 per tick (maxCapturersCounted), so the point is taken after 17 ticks instead of 50.
Five soldiers of side 0 in range count as three: the point is taken after the same 17 ticks as with three.

A soldier of each side stands within the capture radius, one cell below and above the point: they fight and, while both live, the point is contested and no progress is made (no point_capture_started).

A guard soldier holds the point; a drone of side 0 diverts to it (flyers divert too), shoots the guard dead without ever being hit (a melee guard cannot hit a flyer) and, with the guard dead, captures the point.
Two soldiers of side 0 pass a point guarded by one soldier, divert, kill the guard and then capture the point; no progress is made while the guard lives.

A soldier of side 0 takes the point and walks on; a soldier of side 1 comes down the zone later and retakes it (point_captured side 1, previous 0). The ticks each side held the point are in the state.

A soldier of side 0 is capturing when two soldiers of side 1 arrive and kill it: while contested nothing changes, then the progress of side 0 is replaced by that of side 1, which restarts at 0 (a second point_capture_started).

A soldier of side 0 waits two cells below the point and has started capturing it (progress 5) when two soldiers of side 1 divert to the point from the other side and stop two cells above it: four cells apart, beyond the aggro range of 3, nobody fights. The point is contested, so its progress neither grows nor decays for the rest of the run. (A unit pushed closer by later arrivals would start the fight; here nothing arrives.)

One unit_strength point (+20 percent), held by side 0 from tick 0, and a soldier of each side. The soldier of side 0 placed before the point's holder was set (units) has the base health and damage; the soldier of side 0 placed after (lateUnits) has 20 percent more of both; a late soldier of side 1, which holds nothing, has the base. report stats lists [id, hp, maxHp, damage]; pointBonus is [20, 0].
Three unit_strength points all held by side 0 with maxPointStrengthPercent 40: the late soldier of side 0 has 40 percent more health and damage, not 60. pointBonus is [40, 0].
A unit_strength point held by side 1 from tick 0 (side 0 lost it): the late soldier of side 0 is normal, the late soldier of side 1 has +20 percent. pointBonus is [0, 20].

A heal point held by side 0. A side-0 soldier at the point with 10 health (max 40) heals 2 on ticks 0, 10, 20, ...; a soldier of side 0 5 cells away, outside the 3-cell radius, and a soldier of side 1 at the point are not healed. 55 ticks: the healed soldier ends below its max (hp 2 per beat, 6 beats); healed is [12, 0]. Saved and restored once.
A heal point held by side 0 and a soldier of side 0 at 39 of 40 health: the first beat heals 1 (never above the maximum), later beats nothing; healed is [1, 0].
Two heal points of side 0 one cell apart; a soldier within range of both heals 2 per beat, not 4 (healing does not stack): after 25 ticks (beats at 0, 10, 20) it has 6 more health; healed is [6, 0].
A heal point held by side 1: a damaged soldier of side 0 on it is not healed (healed [0, 0]); the point holder's own soldier at 10 health is.

Side 0 holds three Quick march stacks (+30% move speed: soldier and archer move cooldown 6 to 4), side 1 none. Same units at the same cells, so side 0 arrives first; the final positions and the state hash pin the cooldowns (a unit with a changed cooldown carries it in its state).
Side 0 holds Rapid fire (+15% attack speed: soldier and archer attack cooldown 10 to 8), side 1 none. Same units at the same cells; side 0 hits more often.

Both sides have a golem next to a soldier, one cell apart, in the gap. Side 0 holds Stone skin (+1 golem armor: 3 to 4): its golem takes 2 from each soldier hit (6 less 4), side 1's golem takes 3 (6 less 3). The stats report pins the health of every unit and the state hash pins the armor a unit carries (a unit with changed armor has it in its state).

Side 0 holds Wide arcs (+50% caster splash: 50 to 75 percent) and side 1 none. Each side's caster hits one soldier of the other side with a second soldier next to it: the neighbour takes 75 percent of the hit on side 0's cluster of targets and 50 percent on side 1's. The stats report pins the health of every unit.

Side 0 holds Claimstakers (points captured 50% faster: 50 capture ticks become 34). One soldier of side 0 stands on one point and one soldier of side 1 on another; after 40 ticks the first point is held by side 0 (taken at its 34th tick) while the second has progress 39 of 50 for side 1. The run is also saved and restored mid-way.

Two Lancers (reach 300) stand a little behind a soldier each; an enemy soldier stands against each ally. The Lancers hit the enemy over the ally with no targeting rule beyond distance, and hold their place while they do; a drone within reach is never hit (a melee unit cannot hit a flyer).

Four Lancer halls (1x3), one in each rotation (0, 90, 180, 270), each fed by an Ore collector of tier 1, 3, 2 and 1 through its rotated input side (south, west, north, east), make Lancers against a base that makes soldiers. Saved and restored mid-battle.

A tier 2 Grand barracks (3x3) fed by two tier 2 Ore collectors through a Merger spawns two soldiers in the same tick every 56 ticks (4 Ore each, 8 items per production) against a base that makes soldiers. Saved and restored mid-battle.

A tier 1 Grand barracks fed by a tier 3 collector stands in a pen of walls whose only exit cell holds an enemy post (400 health, which the soldiers wear down). The first production spawns two soldiers in one tick; the next finds no room and starts nothing (its 8 items wait); when the post dies two more productions spawn, and the last has room for one soldier only: it spawns that one and holds the other, taking nothing for the next production. Saved and restored while holding.

A tier 2 Mortar (range 10 cells, minimum 3) fed by a tier 3 Ore collector: an enemy Golem held in melee by a friendly Golem about 2 cells from it, inside the blind spot, is ignored for as long as the fight lasts, while a soldier 9.5 cells away is shot (12 damage). Saved and restored mid-battle.

A tier 2 Mortar shells a cluster of five soldiers: the shot unit takes 12 and each other soldier within one cell of it takes floor(12 * 60 / 100) = 7, all in the same tick. Saved and restored mid-battle.

The mortar-splash-group cluster with two Golems among the soldiers: the Golem armor (3) reduces a shot on a Golem to 9 and its splash to 4, soldiers take the splash of 7 (CB-5h: the percent first, then each unit's armor).

Two plots, three unconnected ore extractors each (tiers 1, 2 and 3, intervals 20, 14 and 10; their items are lost at their own cadence). Player 0 picked the Flowmancer (+10 percent collector speed): after the first item their intervals are floor(2000 / 110) = 18, floor(1400 / 110) = 12 and floor(1000 / 110) = 9 (tier 1 items at 19, 37, 55, ...; tier 3 at 9, 18, 27, ...). Player 1 has no specialist and stays on 20, 14 and 10 (CB-51a, EC-8a).

Player 0 is a Flowmancer (+10 percent) and has a tier 3 Overclocker (+5 percent per step, five steps) fed by a fast flux extractor, and an unconnected ore extractor. The specialist bonus is part of the owner's collector speed total, which is capped at 25 percent: the ore extractor starts at 10 percent (interval 18), rises with the steps and stops at 25 (interval 16); the sum never goes beyond the cap (EC-8b).

Both plots have a wall, a one-cell wall, a gate, a tier 2 turret, a tier 2 Mortar and a Barracks; the side holds Stout walls (+25 percent wall health). Player 0 is a Wardsmith (+15 percent on walls, gates and turrets). Player 0's walls have 250 * 140 / 100 = 350 and 100 * 140 / 100 = 140 health (25 and 15 summed, applied once), their gate and turrets +15 percent, their Barracks and Core nothing. Player 1's walls get only the Shrine's 25 percent (312 and 125); nothing else of theirs changes (CB-51a, EC-8a).

Each plot has an ore extractor feeding a Barracks. Player 0 is a Beastbinder (+10 percent unit health): their soldiers spawn with 40 * 110 / 100 = 44 health and the usual damage 6; player 1's soldiers have 40 (CB-51a).

The ramp-armory-stronger-units scenario with a Beastbinder: the soldiers spawned at ticks 99, 199 and 299 have 40 * (100 + 5 * k + 10) / 100 = 46, 48 and 50 health (the Armory's strength and the specialist's health percent are summed and applied once); the soldiers of ticks 399 and 499 have 52 and 54. The damage follows the Armory's strength alone (6, 6, 6, 7, 7).

The ramp-overclocker-own-plot-only scenario with player 0 an Alchemist (+15 percent production speed): their Overclocker takes a step at the earliest every floor(4000 / 115) = 34 ticks instead of 40 (the step size and cap are unchanged); player 1 has no specialist (CB-57).

The refinery-ab-feeds-units scenario with a tier 1 Composite refinery (its two tier 3 collectors fill it faster than its interval) and an Alchemist (+15 percent production speed): the refinery's minimum time between batches is floor(6000 / 115) = 52 ticks instead of 60. Saved and restored at tick 300 like the original (CB-57).

Two plots, three unconnected Mana Wells each on open ground, no node (tiers 1, 2 and 3, intervals 40, 28 and 20). Player 0 picked the Flowmancer: the Extractor bonus (+10 percent collector speed) applies to a Well too, so after the first item their intervals are floor(4000 / 110) = 36, floor(2800 / 110) = 25 and floor(2000 / 110) = 18. Player 1 has no specialist and stays on 40, 28 and 20 (issue #473, CB-51a).

A tier 1 Rune Ward stands in the wall line at (4, 8), powered by its own Extractor, next to the weak wall block (5, 8). An enemy soldier standing at that block hits it every 10 ticks; each hit the Ward holds a charge for returns 2 damage to the soldier in the same tick (`ward_struck` right after `unit_attacked`). A tier 1 Extractor feeds one item per 20 ticks, so the Ward strikes back on about every second hit (issue #474, CB-53).

The control of the Rune Ward vectors: the same wall line with a tier 3 wall block where the Ward stood. Nothing is returned and no `ward_struck` is recorded; the weak block falls to the same soldier (issue #474, CB-53).
The same Rune Ward with no conduit and no supply never holds a charge, so it does nothing: it works only while fed (V-15, CB-10; issue #474, CB-53). The soldier is not struck once.

Two powered tier 1 Rune Wards stand in the wall line at (4, 8) and (6, 8), both sharing an edge with the weak block (5, 8). Each hit on (5, 8) is struck back by one Ward only: the lower building ID that holds a charge. The first Ward spends its charge, so the second takes the next hit while the first refills; the two never strike for the same hit (issue #474, CB-53: no stacking).

A tier 3 Rune Ward (return damage 4) and a golem (armor 3) at the weak block: the strike is reduced by the attacker's armor, `max(1, 4 - 3)` = 1 (CB-5h), unlike the 4 a soldier takes (issue #474, CB-53).

A soldier with 3 health left hits the weak block next to a powered tier 1 Ward: the Ward's first strike (2 damage, tick 30) takes it to 1 and the second (tick 50) kills it: `unit_died` is recorded in the tick of the strike, after the hit of that tick has landed (issue #474, CB-53).

A powered Rune Ward at (3, 8) is two cells from the weak block (5, 8): it shares no edge with it, so a hit on (5, 8) is never struck back (issue #474, CB-53). Its own neighbours (2, 8) and (4, 8) are not attacked.

A powered Rune Ward at (4, 7) is diagonal to the weak block (5, 8) (it shares an edge only with the tier 3 block (4, 8)): a diagonal does not count, so a hit on (5, 8) is never struck back (issue #474, CB-53).

A weak gate (tier 1, health 80) in the wall line at (5, 8) next to a powered tier 1 Rune Ward: a hit on a gate of the Ward's owner is struck back like a hit on a wall (issue #474, CB-53). The soldier is on the enemy's side of the gate, so the gate is closed to it.

Two plots with one wall line across both. The weak block (11, 8) belongs to player 0; a powered tier 1 Rune Ward at (12, 8) shares an edge with it but belongs to player 1 (the partner's plot). A hit on (11, 8) is not struck back: a Ward acts only for walls of its own owner (issue #474, CB-53).

A Beastbinder's Power extractor feeds a tier 1 Familiar Roost (4 Power per Familiar, one every 80 ticks, CB-54). Each Familiar spawns with 20 * 110 / 100 = 22 health and damage 5 (CB-51a), runs at move cooldown 3 (speed 80) and eight of them reach the empty enemy Core and destroy it (500 damage) before tick 700.

A Familiar and a Soldier start side by side the same distance from the enemy Core; the Familiar (move cooldown 3, speed 80) is the first to hit the Core (it has dealt 18 damage after 60 ticks), the raider (cooldown 4) is just behind and the Soldier (move cooldown 6, speed 40) has not arrived.
